steps.content: You're Ji... Cough, cough!

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Hold your breath. Don't move.

Just opening your mouth makes your throat tighten up, sharp burning pain shooting straight to your lungs. Darkness floods your vision, leaving only blurred patches of color and light swaying before your eyes.
Jichuan has led you away from the poison gas and helped you sit down in the clearing behind the mid-lake pavilion.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Purple Haze burns when it meets blood and turns solid in your veins. If you speak now, the poison will follow your breath and attack your heart even faster. Do you have a death wish, young hero?

The way she calls you "young hero" feels strangely familiar. Before you can dwell on it, her palm is already pressed against your back, and a gentle yet irresistible flow of internal force begins to course through you.
You want to turn back to look at her, but her other hand gently presses down on your shoulder.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I told you not to move... If you do, the poison will spread even further.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: The poison in your meridians has already passed three critical points. Delay another moment, and even I won't be able to save you. If you insist on not trusting me... shall I just let you be?
You finally settle down, controlling your breathing and focusing your mind as you sit still as told. The healing process is long and delicate.

Her internal force gradually merges with the Qi flowing through your body, drawing out the poison's chill little by little. You can even sense the rhythm of her breathing clearly. Light and controlled, each breath stirring the air and gently brushing against the strands of loosened hair by your ear.
Strangely, the shackles aren't disturbed by her power, nor do they resist it. A form of indescribable, subtle resonance quietly forms between you during this silent flow of energy.
You lose track of how much time passes, but gradually the tightness in your chest eases, and the burning pain in your throat mostly fades away. Finally, you can speak again.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: ...I was taken by a whim.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Jiewubei and Xu Shen both died gruesomely. At the banquet, you spoke relentlessly. You seemed to be anticipating the bloodshed. Could someone so calculating be so easily "taken by a whim"?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: What about you then? You protected Shuang'er when you were surrounded by those traps. Why was that?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She's not from the same world as those martial heroes, just an ordinary girl who looks up to them. Perhaps you've possessed such extraordinary power for so long that you've forgotten ordinary people have no way to protect themselves from these schemes and conspiracies.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In that situation, I had to find the best solution. Saving her was my instinct in that moment.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Then... this is my instinct too.

You don't understand what she means. Perhaps you've never understood this manor master from the start. The flow of energy between you continues in silence, the poison being slowly drawn like delicate threads from your meridians and absorbed into her body.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I saved you... because you remind me of an old friend.

options: You have friends, even though you've lived in seclusion for years?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I did... when I was very, very young.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I was born with an incurable disease. As a child, I spent most of my days beside the medicine cauldron. I was a burden who could never inherit the manor. I hated the bitter taste and refused to take my medicine, always sneaking out to buy sweets instead... At the town entrance, I met a child around my age.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: She was homeless, yet more spirited than anyone else. Even though we were complete strangers, she would stand in front of my scrawny body and swing her dusty little fists at the bullies.
You feel her internal force growing even gentler, like a spring stream melting ice, flowing warmly through your limbs and meridians.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Together, we made the dishonest butcher return every copper coin he'd overcharged to an old lady, chased off thugs who extorted money from peddlers, and returned a stolen rattle drum to a child from the town.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Back then, I knew little about martial arts, yet I felt... more truly alive than I ever have since.
${PlayerName}

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Are you healing me... because of that old friend?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I failed to keep the promise I made to her. Now, seeing you and Shuang'er... I hope you two can have a better ending.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What promise?

She doesn't answer. The snow falls silently, leaving only the gentle mingling of your breaths. Gradually, the poison recedes. You begin to gradually make out the pavilion corridor before you and feel the warmth of her palm against your back through your clothes.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Bear with me. The superficial poison is cleared, but the residue is still deep in your heart meridian. This final step requires me to guide it out with my Qi, to open your channels and break through the blockage.
You catch the suppressed trembling in her voice. Before you can react, she pushes forcefully with her Qi, and searing pain crashes over you like a tidal wave.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: First your chest will feel frozen, then your limbs will go numb and tingly, followed by a burning sensation in your abdomen... Don't be afraid. These are all normal signs that the poison is being purged. If you feel weak, don't force yourself and just lean against my hand. I'll hold you up.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I already have a lead on who killed the Scholar... And Jiewubei's murder on the first night... that wasn't you either, was it...

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Don't use your internal force within three days after the detoxification. Avoid alcohol and cold foods. Soon after sunset, you should rest and regulate your breathing...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why won't you answer? You brought everyone here... What's your real purpose?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: If you care about your own safety, after the detoxification is complete, just pretend you never saw me here...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you leave the Red Plum Denunciation? You're manipulating these martial heroes. What's your motive behind all this?
Ptuh! You both simultaneously cough up mouthfuls of black blood that splatter horrifyingly across the snow. But what follows is a sudden lightness and clarity washing over your entire body.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That codex of Snowquell Arts...
When you turn around, there's nothing behind you. Only two pools of black blood remain on the snow, like a pair of linked plum blossoms painted with ink.
The bitter wind howls past, sweeping away any lingering traces of her presence. Only the warmth from her palm remains, still burning vividly against your back.
You stand stunned in the snow. On a bare branch nearby, those two little birds appear again, pecking at each other irritably before flying off in opposite directions.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: What's on your mind?
Xiaofeng leaps out of nowhere, and before she's even steadied herself, her hand is already reaching over to grasp your wrist.

steps.speaker: Department Head
steps.content: Looks like someone beat me to playing nice. Hmm, too bad, this "mountain demon" you suspected of heartless murders was just planning to come and heal your injury.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: With the fake claw marks and the traps designed to kill any witnesses, you're cleared of all suspicion in the Scholar's case. I believe we're both aware of that.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're not the one I'm after.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Oh, so now you're cutting ties with me? How cruel!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Where's Shuang'er? Didn't she come out with you?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: She slipped away faster than a mountain sparrow. You'll have to look for her yourself. I need to go back and take a good, long nap.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Aren't we going to confront Ma Ling and ask her why she framed you?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...There won't be a need anymore.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: The General... already died in her own trap.
[Small CG: Dead Body 3]

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: So the righteous general and the protector of the people was nothing but an ambitious schemer underneath. She dug a trap for her enemies and ended up falling into it herself. I suppose... this was an outcome she deserved.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: The human world is indeed inferior to my mountains, where the order of survival is simple and honest!
With these casual musings, she shoulders her wine gourd and strolls away into the distance.
Behind the ornamental rocks, a figure in white stands quietly, watching it all unfold.

As the north wind sweeps by, her complexion appears several shades paler than the snow itself, a sign of the poison still coursing through her system. Yet colder than her ashen face is the gaze with which she watches the manor.

She clutches a scroll in her hand, eyes downcast as she watches the violence slowly subside. The martial world's true nature strips itself bare inch by inch against the bloodied snow, and the last glimmer of light in her eyes finally dies.
Before turning to leave, she raises her hands and ties the Red Plum Denunciation to a withered plum branch.

Red Plum Denunciation III Golden spears and iron steeds now all rust in graves. Arrowheads forged with blood still seek revenge unpaid. In a realm of decay, if a rotten trunk is to hold the sky, the world shall hear no songs of spring, only a muted cry.
